Élections 2025 : « De nombreux Canadiens: Elections 2025: “Many Canadians want to vote for politicians who are able to take a stand on a genocide.”
Les défenseurs des droits des Palestinie: Advocates for Palestinian rights see the election as an opportunity to force the Israeli-Palestinian issue into the political debate.
Les élections battent leur plein au pays: The election campaign is in full swing across the country, and for this first article on the federal vote, I’m looking at an issue that is gradually making its way into Canadian political debate: the Palestinian question.
C’est la première fois que je couvre des: This is the first time I’m covering an election, and I’m thrilled to be doing it here at La Converse. While media attention is largely focused on Donald Trump’s daily pronouncements, other crucial issues, particularly social and humanitarian ones, are struggling to find a place in the campaign. Yet on the ground, mobilizations are intensifying.
Les défenseurs des droits des Palestinie: Advocates for Palestinian rights fully intend to make this issue part of the election. Through Votez Palestine, a non-partisan initiative, they are challenging candidates and voters with five main demands: 1) impose a bilateral arms embargo between Canada and Israel; 2) denounce anti-Palestinian racism and protect freedom of expression in Canada on the Palestinian question; 3) protect and fund humanitarian interventions in Gaza; 4) end Canada’s involvement in illegal Israeli settlements; 5) officially recognize the State of Palestine.
Et leur message trouve un écho de plus e: And their message is resonating more and more: 152 federal candidates already support their platform, including Jagmeet Singh, leader of the NDP, and Elizabeth May, leader of the Green Party.
Alors que les libéraux demeurent en tête: With the Liberals still leading in voting intentions, followed closely by the Conservatives and then the NDP, what place does the Palestinian question really occupy in this election? How are the parties positioning themselves on it? We break it down in this article!
<strong>Depuis le 18 mars, l’armée israé: Since March 18, the Israeli army has resumed its bombing of Gaza, ending the ceasefire put in place in January. The human toll has risen since then, reaching 1,000 dead. Meanwhile, in Canada, a federal election campaign has been underway since March 23. Advocates for Palestinian rights see it as an opportunity to force the Israeli-Palestinian issue into the political debate.
Les mobilisations en soutien à Gaza ne c: Mobilizations in support of Gaza have been growing steadily across the country since October 2023. Demonstrations, petitions, awareness campaigns – a growing share of the Canadian public is demanding that the government take a firmer stand against Israel’s military operations. This movement is also taking political form: voters and activists are organizing to make the Palestinian cause a major electoral issue.
<strong>Jeudi 27 mars. </strong>Haya app: Thursday, March 27. Haya appears on our computer screen. Her smile contrasts with the frustration she says she feels during this election period. The young woman of Palestinian origin is one of the people behind Votez Palestine, a non-partisan campaign that seeks to put the question of Palestinian rights at the heart of the Canadian electoral debate. We meet her by videoconference, as she juggles calls and meetings back to back, barely two weeks after the campaign’s launch.
« Depuis octobre 2023, on a vu que le Ca: “Since October 2023, we’ve seen that Canada is very, very complicit in the Israeli genocide, whether through investments, diplomatic support or the export of weapons and military components,” she begins.
PourVotez Palestine, l’objectif est doub: For Votez Palestine, the goal is twofold. “On the one hand, we want to show that we will no longer tolerate Canada’s complicity. (...) We also want to show that we have a voice that has grown stronger since October 2023,” Haya explains. She then adds: “Voters are the ones with the power to give MPs their seats. If they want our support, they have to listen to us. They have to hear the demands of Canadians, Arabs, Palestinians and Muslims who place this issue at the heart of their concerns.”
« Avec la campagne Votez Palestine, on m: “With the Votez Palestine campaign, we’re showing that this issue doesn’t concern only Palestinians: many Canadians want to vote for politicians who are able to take a stand on a genocide,” she says.
Lancée le 11 mars, <l1>Votez Palestine f: Launched on March 11, <l1>Votez Palestine brings together a network of 135 organizations</l1> – including the Palestinian Youth Movement, the Quebec coalition Urgence Palestine and Independent Jewish Voices – representing nearly 2 million people who officially support the platform, according to the website.
L’initiative suit donc de près les posit: The initiative is therefore closely tracking candidates’ positions and is actively involved in several ridings. Volunteers email candidates to present the demands and invite them to sign on if they agree. These efforts then make it possible to identify those who support Votez Palestine’s demands and to make that information available to voters.

En date du 3 avril, 152 candidats fédéra: As of April 3, 152 federal candidates have declared their support for the Votez Palestine platform: 107 from the New Democratic Party (NDP), 9 from the Liberal Party and 36 from the Green Party. Among them are two prominent political figures: Jagmeet Singh, leader of the NDP, and Elizabeth May, leader of the Green Party, who have publicly endorsed the platform.
« Les politiciens sentent la pression de: “Politicians are feeling the pressure from their voters, and some are finally starting to take a principled position on Palestine,” says Haya.

Parmi ces électeurs qui comptent faire d: Among those voters who intend to make Palestine a central issue in the election is Amina*, a 25-year-old Montrealer who will be voting in only her second federal election.
En 2019, elle avait fait son choix en fo: In 2019, she made her choice based on other criteria. But this time, she feels a break. “Palestine is a big issue in this election. And we’ve seen that the last government played a role in the genocide. We want it to stop.”
D’un ton maussade, elle poursuit : « La: In a gloomy tone, she continues: “Palestine is my red line, because a politician who is silent on or complicit in a genocide, I don’t think they’ll have my interests at heart, as a Palestinian or as a Canadian.” She insists: “I don’t think a politician who turns a blind eye to a genocide can seriously tackle the housing crisis or precarity,” she hammers home. “It’s a question of values!” she exclaims.
Après un soupir, elle reprend : « On vit: After a sigh, she goes on: “We’re living through a difficult time. That’s why we have to demand more from our politicians, more than usual. They need to be a little bit afraid of us. If they don’t respect that, they won’t get our votes.”
Les annonces d’aide humanitaire ne suffi: Announcements of humanitarian aid aren’t enough to convince her. “I saw that Mélanie Joly, the foreign affairs minister, signed off on a $100-million shipment to Gaza. But that doesn’t erase the fact that, during the genocide, she did nothing to stop it. It’s going to take a lot more than that.”
Pour elle, la campagne Votez Palestine e: For her, the Votez Palestine campaign is a new way of demanding accountability. “It’s a key moment. If politicians want our votes, they have to understand that this issue is non-negotiable. We don’t want half-measures anymore. They have to accept each and every one of our demands.”
Elle marque une pause et reprend d’un to: She pauses and goes on in a gloomy tone: “As a Canadian, I don’t want my government to be on the wrong side of history. Our country claims to defend human rights, so now is the time to prove it.”

‍<strong>Résumé de la position du Parti: Summary of the Conservative Party of Canada’s position on Gaza:
Le Parti conservateur du Canada soutient: The Conservative Party of Canada firmly supports Israel’s right to defend itself against Hamas attacks. It does not call for an immediate ceasefire, but advocates temporary humanitarian pauses to evacuate civilians and deliver aid to Gaza.
Pierre Poilievre a affirmé sa position c: Pierre Poilievre has stated his opposition to UNRWA, the UN agency that assists Palestinian refugees, calling it a “terrorist organization” and promising to cut its funding if he becomes prime minister. He sharply criticizes Justin Trudeau for maintaining that support.
Le chef conservateur a aussi rejeté le b: The Conservative leader has also dismissed the merits of the case brought against Israel before the International Court of Justice. In a public address to the Beth Israel Beth Aaron congregation in Montréal, he stated his support for Israel unambiguously. “I am a friend of the State of Israel and I will be a friend of the State of Israel everywhere I go.”
Au troisième jour des élections, son con: On the third day of the campaign, his assessment illustrates the increasingly intense dilemma some voters are facing. A public servant, Tristan prefers to remain anonymous because of his duty of discretion.
« J’ai toujours eu une sensibilité polit: “I’ve always had fairly conservative political leanings. Historically, I’ve voted for the Conservative Party, even though its support for Israel has always been clear,” he explains over the phone. Yet over time and through his personal experiences, his outlook has changed.
Voyageant souvent au Proche-Orient, il c: Travelling often to the Middle East, he understands that on the ground, conflicts are not simply topics of political discussion: they govern people’s daily lives. “We’re talking about an entire region that has been erased in almost 70 years. And now they want to erase what’s left. And Israel openly owns it. What’s ironic is that Western politicians remain silent on the issue.”
Selon lui, « si les dirigeants ne disent: According to him, “if leaders say nothing, it’s for reasons of funding and electoral calculations in various ridings.” He sees the unwavering support for certain Israeli positions as a reflection of behind-the-scenes influence games, much more than a sincere stand.
Cette position l’a poussé à reconsidérer: This stance has led him to reconsider his political choices. While he rules out the NDP, which he considers too far left and removed from his economic and social values, he sees in Mark Carney a more centrist and balanced alternative. “The Liberal Party remains at the centre of the political landscape, especially in a context of polarization. It’s an option that seems more coherent to me,” he says.
<strong>Une politique étrangère canadien: A Canadian foreign policy at odds with its own principles
Antonius Rachad, professeur de sociologi: Antonius Rachad, a retired sociology professor and expert on Middle East conflicts, has watched Canada evolve over his 55 years of living in Quebec. Of Egyptian and Syrian-Lebanese origin, he says he is above all “pro-human rights” and not “pro-Palestinian.” It is through this lens that he analyzes the Canadian position on Gaza.
« Le Canada n’a jamais été une puissance: “Canada has never been a major power in the region; it plays more of a secondary role behind the United States,” the specialist begins. He nonetheless points to its dual approach: “Canada provides humanitarian support to Palestinians, while adopting an ambiguous political position.”
Sur le plan humanitaire, le pays joue en: On the humanitarian front, the country does indeed play a role. Notably, it funds UNRWA (the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East), which provides vital aid to Palestinians. The Canadian International Development Agency (CIDA) has also supported social and economic development projects in the occupied territories.
Mais cette posture entre en contradictio: But this stance contradicts Ottawa’s foreign policy. On paper, Canada presents itself as very close to international law. The website of <l1>Global Affairs Canada</l1> states the following:
« Le Canada reconnaît le droit des Pales: “Canada recognizes the right of Palestinians to self-determination and supports the creation of a sovereign, independent, viable, democratic and territorially contiguous Palestinian state.”
« Le Canada ne reconnaît pas le contrôle: “Canada does not recognize permanent Israeli control over the territories occupied in 1967 (the Golan Heights, the West Bank, East Jerusalem and the Gaza Strip).”
Pourtant, dans les faits, le pays s’alig: Yet in practice, the country aligns itself with Israeli and American interests, relegating the Palestinian cause to the background, the expert notes: “Canada displays its support for the Palestinian people in its official statements, but puts ‘support for Israel and its security’ first on its website. Yet today, it is the security of Palestinians that is most under threat.”
Cet engagement en faveur d’Israël s’est: This commitment to Israel has notably translated into arms shipments to the IDF. <l1>A report published on March 26 by Project Ploughshares</l1> – a Canadian peace research institute – reveals in particular that the Quebec-based company General Dynamics (GD-OTS-Canada) signed a $78.8-million contract in September 2024 to supply artillery propellants (propulsion products) to Israel, even as the bombing of Gaza continued.
Cette entente a été validée par la Corpo: The agreement was validated by the Canadian Commercial Corporation (CCC) on September 26, 2024, barely two weeks after Minister Mélanie Joly blocked the sale of 50,000 “highly explosive” mortar shells <l1>under pressure from human rights advocates</l1>. At the time, she had assured that “no form of weapon” made in Canada would be used in the Gaza Strip, and that the country would prevent any export of weapons or military components that could be used in Gaza, including through the United States.
<strong>Élections canadiennes : un choix: Canadian election: a Cornelian choice for citizens concerned about the situation in Gaza
Face à cette politique ambiguë, que peuv: Faced with this ambiguous policy, what can Canadians concerned about the situation in Gaza hope for? According to Mr. Rachad, the Middle East conflict expert, the outlook is not encouraging.
« Si les conservateurs prennent le pouvo: “If the Conservatives take power, there will no longer be any reference to international law. Support for Israel will be total, and humanitarian aid to Palestinians will disappear,” he says.
D’autre part, il croit que les libéraux: On the other hand, he believes the Liberals may not respond to Israel’s attacks the way advocates for Palestinian rights hope, either. While Justin Trudeau, when he was still prime minister, had declared that an arrest warrant would be issued against Benjamin Netanyahu if he set foot on Canadian soil, Mark Carney remains silent in the face of the resumption of bombing. A silence all the more striking given that two influential figures in his own party, Meyer Weinstein and Marco Mendicino, had voted against the ceasefire. Asked about it, the Prime Minister finally spoke last night, Thursday, April 3, on Radio-Canada: “Territorial integrity is [a right] that cannot be touched. Every effort must be made to restore a ceasefire for Gaza and resume humanitarian aid. The situation in Gaza right now is horrible.” Canadians for Justice and Peace in the Middle East (CJPME) has, moreover, <l1>given Mark Carney a D+ grade</l1> on defending Palestinian rights.
Selon Antonius Rachad, les citoyens préo: According to Antonius Rachad, citizens concerned about the situation in Gaza will therefore have to make a Cornelian choice. Indeed, voting for the NDP – which takes a more critical stance toward Israel – risks being counterproductive, as it could help the Conservatives win. “If the vote splits between Liberals and New Democrats, the Conservatives get through. « Se boucher le nez et voter libéral »,: “Hold your nose and vote Liberal,” the expert advises citizens concerned about the Palestinian question. Not out of inclination, but to “avoid the worst,” he concludes.
